🏢 Social Media for Business Owners · Lesson 4 of 4

From DMs to M-Pesa: Closing the Sale on WhatsApp

7 min read · Updated November 2026 · Free · Written for Kenya
Share: WhatsApp X Facebook Telegram LinkedIn

A Communications Authority survey found WhatsApp and other social channels now carry about 1 in 5 online orders in Kenya — more than traditional websites. Your storefront is a chat window.

Likes don't pay rent. Enquiries that turn into M-Pesa payments do. Most Kenyan businesses lose sales in the gap between "How much?" and "Sent ✅" — slow replies, no prices, unclear payment steps.

~20%
of online orders in Kenya placed via WhatsApp and other social channels; 70%+ of e-commerce done on phones (Communications Authority survey via The Star, Jan 2026)

Set up WhatsApp Business properly (free)

  • Catalogue: up to 500 items, each with photos, price and description. Share the whole thing with one link: wa.me/c/2547XXXXXXXX.
  • Quick replies: type /price, /location, /pay to send saved answers in one tap.
  • Labels: New enquiry → Awaiting payment → Paid → Delivered. You'll see where sales get stuck.
  • Greeting + away messages: answer instantly even when you're busy at the counter.
💡 What most sellers miss

"Inbox me for price" kills sales. Many buyers won't ask — they just leave. Put prices in the catalogue and posts. You lose nothing to competitors who already know your prices, and you stop losing customers who were too shy to ask.

The 4-message close

📋 DM to sale script
1) GREET + QUALIFY: "Karibu! 😊 Is it for you or a gift? Which size/colour?"
2) RECOMMEND + PRICE: "This one is KES 2,500. Here's a photo on a customer 👇"
3) MAKE PAYING EASY: "Pay to Till 123456 ([Business Name]) and I'll confirm right away. Delivery in Westlands today is KES 200."
4) CONFIRM + NEXT STEP: "Received, asante! Rider leaves at 3pm. I'll send his number."
✗ MYTH

WhatsApp is free, so it'll always cost nothing to message customers.

✓ REALITY

The free WhatsApp Business app is still free. But businesses using the WhatsApp Business Platform (API) pay per message, and from 1 October 2026 even service replies are charged after 1,000 free a month (about US$0.0044, ≈ KES 0.57, each in Kenya). Most small shops should stay on the free app until volume truly demands more.

LeakFix
Reply after 3 hoursGreeting message + quick replies; check chats at set times
No price shownPrices in catalogue and posts
"Send to my number"Till/Paybill with business name
Buyer goes quietOne friendly follow-up the next day, then stop
✅ Do this today
⚡ Quick check

What does a wa.me/c/ link do?

wa.me/c/ followed by your number opens your catalogue directly, so a buyer can browse products and prices before messaging — perfect for bios and Status.

🧠 Key takeaways
  1. About 1 in 5 Kenyan online orders now come through WhatsApp and social channels.
  2. A catalogue with prices + quick replies + labels removes most sales leaks.
  3. Make paying easy: a Till with your business name, stated in the chat.
  4. The free app is still free; the API now charges even service replies (from Oct 2026).
